newsitem.title: INDIA: Key Indian economic indicators reflect slowdown.
newsitem.headline: Key Indian economic indicators reflect slowdown.

text.p: India's export growth fell sharply in 1996/97 (April-March) and industrial growth stumbled in the first 10 months, reflecting a worrisome slowdown in the economy, analysts said on Wednesday.

"The trade gap is alarming and growth in exports has been discouraging," said a spokesman for the Federation of Indian Exporters Organisation (FIEO). "We were expecting exports to grow at eight to nine percent."

Exports grew at 4.01 percent to $33.11 billion in 1996/97, compared with 21.38 percent the previous year, the Commerce Ministry announced earlier on Wednesday. Imports in 1996/97 rose to $38.55 billion from $36.37 billion.
The trade deficit widened to $5.44 billion from $4.54 billion the previous year, the ministry said.
Industrial output grew at 7.5 percent in the first 10 months of 1996/97, compared with 11.7 percent in the corresponding period of the previous year.
Industrial production inched ahead by only 1.1 percent in January against 12.9 percent in the same 1996 month, a government statement said.
"Infrastructure bottlenecks are a major cause for slowdown in export and industry," V. Raghuraman, secretary general of the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India, told Reuters.
The FIEO spokesman said: "Imposition of Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT), non-availability of credit and poor infrastructure are major factors for the slowdown in exports."
The controversial MAT -- a 12.9 percent minimum tax on company profits -- was introduced last year to bring some of India's top companies into the tax net.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, moving his 1997/98 budget plan, that would slash corporate and personal income taxes, in parliament on Wednesday, admitted industrial growth was sluggish.
"Industry can and should be growing at a rate of at least 12 percent," Chidambaram said.
"The current slowdown has sharpened the urgency to have the kind of pro-growth, pro-investment budget that was presented on February 28," he added.
The real constraints on a high growth rate are the strictly regulated and under-funded infrastructure sectors of power, petroleum, telecommunications, roads and ports, Chidambaram said.
